mainTopic: Is the levirate bond (זיקה) real? Testing רב יהודה's ruling, challenges from the משנה and a ברייתא, and רבי מאיר's view on losing the מצוה of יבום.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an explanation: רב יהודה needed to teach that the זיקה does not just vanish when the יבמה dies. A ברייתא that permits a dead יבמה's sister is offered as support for him, but the proof is pushed off because the wording only copies the ברייתא's first clause. רב הונא בר חייא then challenges the idea of יש זיקה from our משנה about מאמר. רבה answers that even without מאמר the second wife only does חליצה, and that the משנה mentions מאמר only to reject בית שמאי. אביי challenges again from a ברייתא that allows יבום, and the גמרא answers that this ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who holds אין זיקה. That answer is tested against a משנה about two sisters, where רבי מאיר forbids יבום only out of fear that the מצוה will be lost. When רבן גמליאל is brought up as someone who does not worry about losing the מצוה, רבה explains that the two תנאים can be at opposite extremes. Finally, אביי tells רב יוסף that רב יהודה's ruling comes from שמואל and begins quoting a משנה to show it, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the ruling was needed: the bond does not end by itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why רב יהודה had to say his ruling. Otherwise we might think the זיקה ends when the יבמה dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: I might have thought the bond only exists while she is alive, but once she dies the bond is gone. So he teaches us that a bond does not end for no reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to the question 'Why didn't רב יהודה just say the הלכה follows the view that there is זיקה?' about his ruling that the יבם may not marry his dead יבמה's mother. It explains what new idea the ruling teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the ruling, we might have said the זיקה only works while the יבמה is alive, and her death cancels it. רב יהודה teaches that the זיקה stays in place until a real act ends it, like יבום or חליצה. Death alone does not end it.

keyTerms.meaning: The levirate bond linking the widow to her dead husband's brother
I would have thought (the mistaken first assumption)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole section. If the זיקה lasts even after death, it is a strong, marriage-like bond, and the rest of this part tests that idea.

phrases.english: I would have said: while she is alive,
phrases.notes: This finishes the answer to 'why not just say יש זיקה?' asked just before this part. 'She' is the יבמה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לְאַחַר מִיתָה — פָּקְעָה לַהּ זִיקָה,
phrases.english: but after death the bond is dissolved,
so he teaches us
that a bond does not dissolve for no reason.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question 'why not just say יש זיקה?' raised just before this part about רב יהודה's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the ruling teaches something new (חידוש)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The זיקה exists only while the יבמה is alive and ends at her death.
steps.terutzMaskana: The זיקה does not end by itself. It stays until something actually ends it.

steps.title: A possible proof from a ruling about the dead יבמה's sister
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a ברייתא supports רב יהודה, because it permits only the sister of a dead יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him? 'If his יבמה died, he is permitted to marry her sister.' Her sister, yes. Her mother, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that seems to back up רב יהודה. It reads the teaching closely to show that the mother of the dead יבמה stays forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching says only that the sister is permitted after the יבמה dies. Since it mentions only the sister, it seems to mean the mother is still forbidden. That would match רב יהודה, who holds the זיקה makes the יבמה's mother forbidden even after her death.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?
His יבמה, the widow bound to him

phrases.english: Shall we say it supports him:
If his יבמה died, he is permitted to her sister.
Her sister, yes; her mother, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the meaning of the ruling is clear, the גמרא looks for a source to support it.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's ruling that the dead יבמה's mother stays forbidden because of the זיקה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that permits only the sister after the יבמה dies, which seems to leave the mother forbidden.

steps.title: The proof is rejected: the wording just copies the first clause
steps.stepSummary: The mother may really be permitted too. The ברייתא said 'sister' only to match its first clause about a man's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same is true even for her mother. But since the first part taught 'if his wife died, he is permitted to her sister', which means only her sister and not her mother because the mother is forbidden by the Torah, the last part also said 'he is permitted to her sister'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. It says we cannot learn anything from the word 'sister', because the ברייתא was only repeating the style of its first clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first clause, about a man's own wife who died, mentioning only the sister is exact, because a wife's mother is forbidden by the Torah forever. The second clause, about a יבמה, used the same wording to match. So it does not show that the יבמה's mother is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it taught the first clause (so it used matching wording)

steps.confusionAlert: The two clauses look the same but mean different things. For a wife, 'sister only' is exact, because her mother is forbidden by the Torah. For a יבמה, 'sister' is just copied wording, and the mother may be permitted too.

phrases.english: The same is true even for her mother,
but since he taught in the first clause:
'If his wife died, he is permitted to her sister,'
which means specifically her sister, but not her mother,
since that is a Torah prohibition,
he also taught in the last clause 'permitted to her sister.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not prove רב יהודה wrong.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'sister' in the last clause is not exact. It copies the wording of the first clause, where it is exact.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: without מאמר, the second wife could do יבום
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חייא reads the משנה closely. It seems to allow יבום without מאמר, which does not fit with יש זיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חייא objected: 'If he made a מאמר with her and died, the second wife does חליצה and not יבום.' The reason is that he made a מאמר. But if he had not made a מאמר, the second wife could do יבום. Now if you say יש זיקה, she should count as the צרה of the wife of a brother he never lived alongside, through the bond!
steps.whatsHappening: A challenge is raised against the idea that the זיקה is a real bond. It comes from a careful reading of our משנה about אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה's case, one brother dies childless, and the second brother makes a מאמר with the widow. Only after that is a new brother born, and then the second brother dies. The משנה says the second brother's own wife does חליצה only because of the מאמר. That suggests that without a מאמר she could do יבום. But if the זיקה alone already links the widow to the second brother, his wife should be her צרה and forbidden from יבום even without a מאמר.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic betrothal of the יבמה before יבום
The wife of a brother who died before this brother was born

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Ḥiyya objected:
'If he made a levirate betrothal with her and died,'
phrases.notes: 'He' is the second brother, and 'her' is the first brother's widow. This is from our משנה.

phrases.english: 'the second wife does חליצה and not יבום.'
phrases.notes: The 'second' is the second brother's own wife.

phrases.english: The reason is that he made a מאמר with her;
but if he had not made a מאמר with her,
the second could also do יבום,
and if you say the bond is real,
she is the co-wife of the wife of his brother
who was not in his world, through the bond!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the proof attempt behind and attacks the main idea of יש זיקה from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the זיקה is a real, marriage-like bond (יש זיקה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes the מאמר the reason for the ruling. That implies the זיקה alone would not make the second wife a צרה, which goes against יש זיקה.

steps.title: רבה: even without מאמר, the second wife only does חליצה
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the משנה's mention of מאמר is not exact. Even with no מאמר, the second wife does חליצה and not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The same is true even if he did not make a מאמר with her. The second wife does חליצה but does not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge. He denies the close reading of the משנה, so there is no conflict with יש זיקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא בר חייא assumed the מאמר was the key reason in the משנה. רבה says the ruling is the same without it. The זיקה by itself makes the second wife a צרה, so she does חליצה but cannot do יבום.
steps.whatToRemember: The זיקה stays in force even after the יבמה dies (רב יהודה). The ברייתא about the sister does not prove this. רבה answers the challenge from the משנה by saying that the זיקה alone, even without מאמר, keeps the second wife from יבום.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
The same is true even though
he did not make a מאמר with her:
the second does חליצה,
but does not do יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: הוּא הַדִּין דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא עֲבַד בַּהּ מַאֲמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הונא בר חייא's challenge from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the close reading of the משנה, saying the detail is not exact
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מאמר is the reason, so without it the second wife could do יבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even without מאמר, the זיקה makes the second wife a צרה, so she does חליצה only.

steps.title: Why the משנה mentioned levirate betrothal
steps.stepSummary: רבה finishes his answer. The משנה mentioned מאמר only to reject בית שמאי, who say מאמר is a full קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason the משנה mentions מאמר is to reject בית שמאי, who say מאמר acquires the woman fully. The משנה teaches us that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה just said the word מאמר in the משנה is not exact. Now he explains why the משנה mentioned it anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold that מאמר makes a full marriage bond. If so, the second wife would be a real צרה of a forbidden woman and would be free even from חליצה. By mentioning מאמר, the משנה teaches that even after מאמר she still needs חליצה, so מאמר is not a full קנין.

keyTerms.meaning: to exclude, to reject a certain view

phrases.english: And the fact that it teaches levirate betrothal
is to exclude the view of Beit Shammai,
who say: levirate betrothal makes a full acquisition —
it teaches us that this is not so.
phrases.notes: The point is that even after מאמר she still needs חליצה, so the bond is not complete.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּקָתָנֵי מַאֲמָר, לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִבֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבה's answer from step 5 by explaining why the משנה mentions מאמר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the purpose of an extra detail in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the mention, we might follow בית שמאי and think that after מאמר she is a full צרה and free even from חליצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: מאמר is not a full קנין. The second wife does חליצה, and the משנה still fits יש זיקה.

steps.title: אביי's challenge from a case with no levirate betrothal
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא where no מאמר was done and the second wife may even do יבום. That does not fit יש זיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two brothers lived at the same time. One died childless. The second wanted to do מאמר with the widow but did not manage before a new brother was born, and then he died too. The first widow is free, because she is the wife of a brother the new brother never lived alongside. The second widow may do חליצה or יבום. But if יש זיקה, the second widow should be a צרה of that forbidden woman through the זיקה!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the view that יש זיקה, using a ברייתא that matches the משנה's case but with no מאמר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If יש זיקה, the first widow was tied to the second brother before he died. That would make his own wife her צרה, and the צרה of a forbidden woman cannot do יבום. Yet the ברייתא allows the second wife יבום, which suggests the זיקה is not real.

keyTerms.meaning: he objected to him, citing a source
wife of a brother he never lived alongside; she is exempt from יבום
the levirate bond is a real, binding tie

steps.confusionAlert: Here no מאמר was done at all. That is exactly the case where רבה said the second wife still needs only חליצה, so this ברייתא clashes with him.

phrases.english: Abaye objected to him:
Two brothers who were alive at the same time,
and one of them died without children,
and this second one got up
to do levirate betrothal with his yevama,
but did not manage to do levirate betrothal with her
before a brother was born to him, and then he died.
phrases.notes: The second brother had his own wife. Now both widows fall to the newborn brother.

phrases.english: The first woman goes free

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּעוֹלָמוֹ,
phrases.english: because she is the wife of his brother who was not alive in his lifetime,
and the second either does chalitza or enters levirate marriage.
But if you say the levirate bond is real,
she becomes a rival wife of the wife of his brother
who was not alive in his lifetime, through the bond!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer (and רב יהודה's יש זיקה) with a ברייתא that allows יבום when no מאמר was done.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's ruling that יש זיקה, as defended by רבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If יש זיקה, the second wife is a צרה of a forbidden woman and should be barred from יבום. The ברייתא allows יבום.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is the view of רבי מאיר, who holds אין זיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי מאיר, who says the levirate bond is not real.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יהודה by saying אביי's ברייתא follows a different תנא, רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא really does assume אין זיקה, but that is only רבי מאיר's view. רב יהודה can follow the other view, יש זיקה, so the ברייתא no longer disproves him.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנא, student of רבי עקיבא
the levirate bond is not a real tie

phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Meir,
who said: the levirate bond is not real.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי by assigning the ברייתא to רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the source to a specific תנא with a different view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is everyone's view and disproves יש זיקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is רבי מאיר's view (אין זיקה). רב יהודה follows the opposing view.

steps.title: Does רבי מאיר really hold there is no bond? The four brothers case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the answer by quoting a משנה about two sisters married to two brothers. They must do חליצה and may not do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי מאיר really hold אין זיקה? Didn't we learn: four brothers, two of them married to two sisters. If the husbands of the sisters died, these women do חליצה and not יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer by bringing a משנה that seems to show רבי מאיר holds יש זיקה. This step sets up the source; the next step explains the attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unnamed משנה is assumed to follow רבי מאיר. This משנה forbids יבום for both sisters, which looks like each sister is tied to every surviving brother through זיקה.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't we learn in a משנה?

phrases.english: But does Rabbi Meir really hold
that the levirate bond is not real?
But didn't we learn:
Four brothers,
two of whom are married to two sisters,
and the ones married to the sisters died —
these women do chalitza and do not enter levirate marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי סְבִירָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר אֵין זִיקָה? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 8 that רבי מאיר holds אין זיקה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי מאיר holds אין זיקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה that follows רבי מאיר forbids יבום for two sisters, which seems to need יש זיקה.

steps.title: Without a bond, each brother could marry one sister
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the challenge: if אין זיקה, each sister comes from a different house, so each surviving brother could do יבום with one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think רבי מאיר holds אין זיקה, these sisters come from two separate houses. Let this brother do יבום with one, and that brother do יבום with the other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out why the four-brothers משנה shows that רבי מאיר holds יש זיקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without זיקה, each widow is linked only to whichever brother takes her, so no one ends up with two sisters. The only reason to forbid יבום is that each sister is tied to both brothers. Then each brother is tied to his wife's sister, which is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: and if it enters your mind (to think)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא seems to fit only אין זיקה, but the four-brothers משנה (assumed to be רבי מאיר) seems to show יש זיקה. The next step answers this: רבי מאיר holds אין זיקה and forbids יבום for a different reason.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that Rabbi Meir holds the levirate bond is not real,
these women come from two different houses,
phrases.notes: Each sister was married to a different brother.

phrases.english: so this brother should take one in levirate marriage
and that brother should take the other one!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ סָבַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר אֵין זִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of step 9 by showing why the משנה implies יש זיקה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי מאיר holds אין זיקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without זיקה there is no reason to forbid יבום, since each brother could take one sister. The ban shows each sister is bound to both brothers.

steps.title: רבי מאיר holds no bond, but fears losing the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר really holds אין זיקה. He forbids יבום with the two sisters for a different reason: one brother might die and the מצוה of יבום would be lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, there is no זיקה. רבי מאיר holds that it is forbidden to cancel the מצוה of יבום. Maybe while one brother is doing יבום, the other brother dies, and then the מצוה of יבום is lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 10. The sisters need חליצה and not יבום for a reason that has nothing to do with זיקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture this: the first surviving brother marries one sister through יבום, and then the second surviving brother dies. Now the other sister falls to the first brother, but she is his wife's sister (אחות אשה), so he cannot do יבום with her. To stop that from happening, רבי מאיר says not to do יבום at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually: we keep our original position
The yibum bond between the widow and her husband's brother
To cause the מצוה of יבום to be lost

steps.confusionAlert: The ban on יבום here does NOT come from זיקה. It comes from a worry about what might happen later, namely that the other brother might die.

phrases.english: Really, there is no zika (bond).
Because he (רבי מאיר) holds
that it is forbidden to cancel the מצוה of yibum —
for perhaps while one (brother) is doing yibum,
the other (brother) dies,
and you end up canceling the מצוה of yibum.
phrases.notes: The second sister would then fall to a brother already married to her sister, so she is forbidden to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 10 by giving a different reason for the ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new reason for the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on יבום shows that רבי מאיר holds יש זיקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר holds אין זיקה. He bans יבום only so the מצוה is not lost if a brother dies.

steps.title: If there is no bond, let the מצוה be lost
steps.stepSummary: If there is no זיקה, why worry about losing the מצוה? רבן גמליאל holds אין זיקה and allows the מצוה to be canceled.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is no זיקה, let the מצוה be canceled! After all, רבן גמליאל said: there is no זיקה, and it is permitted to cancel the מצוה of יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 11. It points out that רבן גמליאל, who also holds אין זיקה, is not worried about losing the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is no real bond, the obligation of יבום is weak, so losing it should not matter. רבן גמליאל seems to link the two ideas: no זיקה means you may cancel the מצוה. So why would רבי מאיר worry?

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who holds אין זיקה

phrases.english: But if there is no zika — let it be canceled!
For Rabban Gamliel said:
There is no zika,
and it is permitted to cancel the מצוה of yibum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי מאיר holds אין זיקה and still worries about canceling the מצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If there is no זיקה, there is no reason to protect the מצוה. רבן גמליאל shows the two ideas go together.

steps.title: The source for רבן גמליאל's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה where רבן גמליאל lets the adult sister go free because she is the wife's sister. He does not worry about losing the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבן גמליאל says: if she refused, she refused. If she did not refuse, let her wait until she grows up, and then the other sister goes free because she is the wife's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה that proves what רבן גמליאל holds, to support the challenge in Step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two brothers married two sisters. One sister is an orphaned minor. The adult sister's husband died, so she falls to the minor's husband. רבן גמליאל does not force the minor to refuse her marriage (מיאון) so that יבום can happen. He lets the adult sister go free, which means he is fine with the מצוה being lost.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
She refused: a minor girl canceling her rabbinic marriage (מיאון)
Wife's sister: forbidden, so she is exempt from יבום

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabban Gamliel says:
If she refused — she refused,
and if she did not refuse —
let her wait until she grows up,
and that one goes free, because she is a wife's sister.
phrases.notes: "That one" is the adult widow. Once the minor is fully his wife, her sister is completely off-limits to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the view of רבן גמליאל cited in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן גמליאל permits canceling the מצוה of יבום
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on יבמות 109a about the minor and adult sisters

steps.title: You can't compare two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבה pushes back: why ask a question on רבי מאיר from רבן גמליאל? They are two different תנאים who can disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רבה) said to him: are you throwing רבן גמליאל against רבי מאיר?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה rejects the challenge. Two different תנאים are allowed to hold different views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A question only works if it shows that the same person contradicts himself. רבן גמליאל and רבי מאיר are separate תנאים, so a difference between them proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: You are throwing / setting against (raising a contradiction)

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבה is answering אביי, who has been asking the questions.

phrases.english: Are you throwing Rabban Gamliel's view against Rabbi Meir's?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of Steps 12 and 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole challenge from רבן גמליאל
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It compares two different תנאים, who are allowed to disagree.

steps.title: אביי explains: the gap is too big
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains his point. It is strange that רבי מאיר worries even about a doubtful loss of the מצוה, while רבן גמליאל does not worry even about a certain loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, this is what we mean: רבי מאיר worries even about a doubt, while רבן גמליאל does not worry even about a certainty!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי clarifies his question. He is not claiming a contradiction. He is saying the two opinions are too far apart to make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי מאיר's case, the loss depends on a brother maybe dying, so it is only a ספק. In רבן גמליאל's case, the loss is definite. Both hold אין זיקה, so how can one be so strict and the other so lenient?

keyTerms.meaning: This is what we are saying

phrases.english: No, this is what we are saying:
Rabbi Meir worries even about a doubt,
phrases.notes: The doubt is whether a brother will die before the second יבום happens.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אֲפִילּוּ לְוַדַּאי לָא חָיֵישׁ!
phrases.english: while Rabban Gamliel doesn't worry even about a certainty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the challenge so that רבה's pushback in Step 14 no longer applies.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation of רבי מאיר in Step 11
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two תנאים who agree on אין זיקה should not be at opposite extremes about canceling the מצוה.

steps.title: Such a gap is possible
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the two opinions can really be that far apart. Whoever does not worry at all ignores even a certain loss. Whoever does worry worries even about a doubtful one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps whoever is not concerned is not concerned even about a certainty, and whoever is concerned is concerned even about a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי's question. Extreme positions on both sides make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two תנאים disagree on a basic question: does the loss of the מצוה of יבום matter at all? If it does not matter, even a certain loss is fine. If it does matter, even a possible loss must be avoided. So the explanation of רבי מאיר holds up.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר holds אין זיקה, yet he forbids יבום with the two sisters because he fears even a possible loss of the מצוה. רבן גמליאל, who also holds אין זיקה, does not mind even a certain loss.

phrases.english: Perhaps the one who is not concerned —
is not concerned even about a certainty,
and the one who is concerned —
is concerned even about a doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's clarified challenge in Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the two opinions are a basic disagreement, so extreme positions are logical
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two תנאים holding אין זיקה cannot be so far apart.
steps.terutzMaskana: They disagree on whether losing the מצוה matters at all, so one is fully lenient and the other fully strict.

steps.title: אביי says רב יהודה's ruling comes from שמואל
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רב יוסף that רב יהודה's ruling (even after the יבמה dies, her mother is still forbidden to the יבם) is the view of שמואל. He then begins to bring a משנה as evidence.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: This ruling of רב יהודה is really the opinion of שמואל, as we learned in a משנה:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the argument between רב הונא and רב יהודה, and אביי says which teacher רב יהודה learned his ruling from. This line sets up the next move: the word דִּתְנַן tells us a משנה is about to be quoted as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה learned from two teachers, רב and שמואל. אביי claims this ruling about the יבמה's mother comes from שמואל, not from רב. He has not proven it yet; the proof will come from the משנה quoted next.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes from שמואל (it is his opinion)
As we learned in a משנה (introduces a quote from a משנה)
A widow waiting for יבום with her late husband's brother

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think אביי is starting a new topic. He is going back to the earlier argument between רב הונא and רב יהודה about the dead יבמה's mother, which the side discussion had interrupted.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
This ruling of Rav Yehuda
phrases.notes: He means the ruling that even after the יבמה dies, her mother is still forbidden to the יבם.

phrases.english: is from Shmuel.
As we learned in a mishna:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף: הָא דְּרַב יְהוּדָה — דִּשְׁמוּאֵל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about רבי מאיר and רבן גמליאל (steps 12-16) and goes back to the main argument between רב הונא and רב יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה's ruling, that the dead יבמה's mother stays forbidden to the יבם, is the opinion of שמואל, not רב. A משנה is about to be brought to show this.
